question: Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar non-ketotic coma:

options.opa: It has an effective plasma osmolarity> 320 mOsm / Kg.
options.opb: It always implies the need for insulin treatment after healing.
options.opc: It needs an important contribution of bicarbonate for its treatment.
options.opd: It is a common form of presentation of juvenile diabetes.

analysis: Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar non-ketotic coma is characterized by very high blood glucose levels and effective plasma osmolarity greater than 320 mOsm/Kg. Treatment involves fluid resuscitation and correction of electrolyte imbalances, but not necessarily always requiring insulin therapy or significant bicarbonate contribution. It is more commonly seen in older individuals with type 2 diabetes rather than juvenile diabetes.
